evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The manager_restarted predicate only requires positive, different PIDs and nonempty, different invocation IDs. If the guest reboots between the two manager snapshots, both values change because the service starts in a new boot, so the predicate passes even though the observations do not prove an isolated manager restart. The reboot snapshots already carry boot_id, so requiring the two manager snapshots to have nonempty equal boot_id (while keeping the PID/invocation checks) is the minimal correction.
